short: Diff-E-style decoder (M06) whose own ablation does not show diffusion helping; 1.01-point imagined-speech gain over EEGNet on two held-out subjects, normalized on scored trials (M03).
position: MultiDiffNet [@zhang2025multidiffnet] changes the decoder (M06) and the evaluation protocol (M12); both are standard. The decoder continues the Diff-E design of a diffusion model trained with an autoencoder and a latent classifier [@kim2023diffe], but the paper's own ablation does not support the claim that diffusion drives generalization: the configuration without the diffusion model scores 13.76% on unseen imagined-speech subjects against 11.62% for the full model (Tables 13 and 17), the reverse of the within-subject drops reported for this design family [@kim2023diffe; @kim2024ensemble]. The base model gains 1.01 points over EEGNet on two held-out imagined-speech subjects (1.51 with Mixup), and unseen-subject normalization takes label-free statistics from trials that are then scored (M03, not reported in the paper).
